characterization_methods.key_findings: The degree of dynamic recrystallization ranked: zone 3 (large deformation) > zone 2 (small deformation) > zone 1 (difficult deformation); DRX degree increases with temperature and with decreasing strain rate.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Compressed sample split in half along the axial axis, prepared by grinding, polishing and etching; etchant: 30% nitric acid alcohol solution (volume fraction).
characterization_methods.purpose: Collect microstructure images of the three deformation zones after hot compression to analyse microstructure evolution and DRX.

characterization_methods.key_findings: The steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive material; the flow/peak stress increases with increasing strain rate or decreasing temperature.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Temperatures 900–1150 °C, strain rates 0.01–10 s^-1, maximum compression 60% (true strain 0.92).
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure rheological (flow) stress curves to analyse hot deformation behaviour and DRX of the steel.
characterization_methods.technique: isothermal constant-strain-rate hot compression testing (flow-stress measurement)

analytical_models.equation_role: Relate peak stress, temperature and strain rate to determine the DRX activation energy Qp.
analytical_models.model_note: Qp = 1000·R·k1·k2; reported as the average value within the experimental range (900–1150 °C, 0.01–10 s^-1) for the Fe-Mn-Al-C steel.

analytical_models.equation_role: Temperature-compensated strain-rate parameter; lnZ value for this sample.
analytical_models.model_note: Table 1 gives lnZ = 66.38 at T = 900 °C and ε̇ = 0.1 s^-1 (this sample's condition).

computational_details.simulation_method: Arrhenius hyperbolic-sine constitutive analysis with Zener-Hollomon parameter

analytical_models.equation_role: Relate critical, peak and steady-state strains/stresses of the flow curve to lnZ.
analytical_models.model_name: DRX characteristic value models vs lnZ (Eq. 10)
analytical_models.model_note: Regression fits (R between 0.911 and 0.957 for the six characteristic values). εc/εp ≈ 0.452; material constant C at 1050 °C/0.01 s^-1 = 0.1461 (R = 0.9728).

computational_details.simulation_method: Multiple linear regression fitting of DRX characteristic values versus lnZ (Cingara-McQueen method for critical strain).

analytical_models.equation_role: Predict DRX average grain size from strain rate, temperature and material constants.
analytical_models.model_name: DRX average grain size prediction model (Eq. 12)
analytical_models.model_note: General DRX grain-size model for the steel (Eq. 11 form d_rex = a·d0^h·ε^p·ε̇^q·exp(Q/RT) + b, with initial grain size and strain treated as constants).

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Billet set as a rigid-plastic body, die indenter as a rigid body; semi-symmetric specimen used as deformation model; friction at billet-die contact set as shear type with value 0.3; convection coefficient of billet and air = 0.02 N/(s·mm·°C); simulation matched the thermal-compression experimental conditions.
computational_details.simulation_method: Levenberg-Marquardt regression of the experimental DRX average grain-size data; finite-element modelling with DEFORM-3D.
computational_details.software_used: DEFORM-3D (finite element software); Levenberg-Marquardt optimization algorithm
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Predicted versus experimental grain size: correlation coefficient R = 0.996 and MRE = 4.53%; absolute error mostly within 3 µm.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Sample heated to 1200 °C at a rate of 10 °C/s.
Homogenized by holding at 1200 °C for 120 s.
Cooled from 1200 °C to the set temperature (900 °C) at a rate of 5 °C/s.
Held for 15 s at the set temperature (900 °C) before compression so the temperature difference between inside and outside of the sample was the same.

Isothermal constant strain rate compression at 900 °C and 0.1 s^-1 (the strain-rate condition of this sample) to a 60% reduction (true strain 0.92); performed on a Gleeble-3500 thermo-mechanical simulator.
After compression, the sample was sprayed with water to cool the steel down (quenching).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Isothermal constant-strain-rate compression to a maximum of 60% (true strain 0.92); Gleeble-3500 thermo-mechanical simulator; mica foils with high-temperature lubricant on the two end faces.

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Large polygonal grains — individual grains span roughly one to a few times the 100 µm scale bar; no numeric grain-size value is printed.

microstructure_list.region: initial (pre-deformation bulk of the forging billet)

structures.overall_structure: Initial as-forged microstructure of the FeeMneAleC steel billet before hot compression: large polygonal grains delimited by bright etched boundaries (a bright, continuous, slightly etched network), with dark grey grain interiors containing abundant fine, closely spaced, parallel light-grey striations/lamellae (segregation banding); some grains almost featureless and light grey while others are densely striped, indicating chemical heterogeneity in the as-forged condition.

microstructure_list.region: core / large deformation zone (region 3) of the compressed specimen

structures.overall_structure: Post-compression (60% hot compression) dynamically recrystallized structure of the sample at 900 °C / 0.1 s^-1, observed in the core (large deformation zone). General DRX behavior for this steel: at low temperature the DRX grains are small but the recrystallization is not sufficient and large original grains remain, so microstructure homogeneity is comparatively poor; the degree of DRX increases with increasing temperature and decreasing strain rate. No dedicated micrograph for the 900 °C/0.1 s^-1 condition is shown; Fig. 9 panels cover 1100 °C (0.01/0.1/10 s^-1) and 950/1050/1150 °C (1 s^-1).

unmapped_findings: FeeMneAleC steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive material: its rheological (flow) stress increases with increasing strain rate or decreasing temperature, so peak stress can be reduced by decreasing strain rate or increasing temperature (b0021, b0024, b0084).

Recommended hot-working window for a fine and uniform grain structure: 950–1000 °C/0.01–0.1 s^-1 and 1050–1100 °C/1–10 s^-1; the present 900 °C/0.1 s^-1 condition lies outside (below) this window (b0065, b0086).
The critical-to-peak strain ratio for DRX of this steel is εc/εp ≈ 0.452, consistent with literature values from the θ–σ inflection-point method (b0054).

For the 0.01 s^-1 strain rate, peak stress decreased from 305.4 MPa at 900 °C to 53.8 MPa at 1150 °C (an 82% reduction); at 10 s^-1 the peak stress decreased by 73% over the same temperature range (b0024).
The initial (as-forged) grain size of the billet is not reported numerically; Fig. 1 shows large polygonal grains with fine parallel segregation striations (figure_001).

Compression produces a non-uniform stress field with three deformation zones: 1 – difficult deformation zone, 2 – small deformation zone, 3 – large deformation zone; the DRX degree ranks zone 3 > zone 2 > zone 1 (b0060, b0063, figure_008).

The compression tests on the same FeeMneAleC steel batch/composition were confirmed under identical experimental conditions to check reproducibility; the reported experimental phenomena are stated to have reproducibility (b0018, b0024, b0037, b0058, b0065).
